## Exercises (sample)

1. Any number of parameters (including zero).
2. Avoid duplicating long expressions; reuse from multiple advice methods.
3. JDK proxies implement interfaces only — the runtime object is not an instance of your concrete class.
4. The call never enters the proxy; it goes straight to the target method on `this`.
5. `AopUtils.isAopProxy(bean)` (and related helpers) or inspect `bean.getClass()`.

## Self-check

1. Example: `execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))`.
2. **False.** Spring AOP focuses on external calls to Spring beans (typically public API through the proxy).
3. **CGLIB**.
4. `@Pointcut`.
